title: In the LLM era, Word Sense Induction remains unsolved

selection.evidence: Web search 2026-11-06 for LLM sense induction while pre-registering arena-lsc ticket 2026-11-06-InventoryBreadth (an LLM-induced inventory for SemEval-2027 Task 3). The only 2026 paper found that evaluates direct LLM WSI.

cost.compute_notes: PDF pp. 1-9 read in full (sec. 1-8, Tables 1-6); appendices not read. Repo cloned (112 MB, mostly augmentation csvs). r01 runs in ~20 s CPU.

triggers: one cluster per lemma baseline unbeaten
word sense induction natural polysemy distribution
direct LLM prompting for WSI fails
number of clusters from a lexicon (Wiktionary) beats silhouette
data augmentation with unlabeled corpus examples for WSI

claims.statement: On SemCor-WSI (SemCor lemmas sampled to keep the corpus polysemy and frequency distribution; dev 15,308 instances / 1,271 lemmas), no unsupervised system beats one-cluster-per-lemma (1cpl) on instance-weighted F-B3: 1cpl 73.6 dev (verb 65.7, adj 80.0, noun 75.2), 74.4 test; PolyLM-large 73.0 dev / 72.7 test; best embedding clustering 71.1-71.8 dev.
claims.scope: English, SemCor 3.0 brown1+brown2, WordNet senses, first sense kept for multi-sense instances. Weighted F-B3 (by instances).

our_assessment.why: 1cpl rows reproduce from the released csvs (dev all/verb/adj/noun 73.6/65.7/80.0/75.2 exactly; test 74.5 vs printed 74.4); 1cpex is 0.2-0.5 below print (unexplained, small). The headline is arithmetic of the sample, made explicit by r01: 28.1% of dev instances (54.8% of lemmas) belong to monosemous lemmas, where 1cpl is perfect; on polysemous lemmas alone 1cpl scores 63.4 (test 65.2). So 'nothing beats 1cpl' means 'nothing beats 63.4 on polysemous lemmas without splitting monosemous ones'. It does not transfer to target-word benchmarks chosen for polysemy or change (SemEval-2027 Task 3 SV dev: 1cpl 1a 0.756 vs XL-LEXEME clustering 0.82).

claims.statement: Direct LLM prompting (all instances of a lemma in one prompt, the LLM returns clusters) is far below clustering: SemCor-WSI F-B3 Llama 3.1 8B 59.7, Llama 3.3 70B 4-bit 64.2, GPT-4o 66.9 vs 1cpl 73.6; Llama loses the task beyond ~300 examples. Their Future Work (i) proposes 'ask for a list of senses, then assign instances to them'.
claims.scope: Table 2; one prompt per lemma, five runs.

our_assessment.why: As printed (not rerun: needs an API or a 70B model). The induce-then-assign design they leave as future work is what arena-lsc runs (Gemma 4 12B, tooling/llm_inventory.py): on SemEval-2027 Task 3 SV dev it also LOSES on BCubed (0.653 vs 0.823) while gaining on 1b (F9 in arena-lsc paper/FINDINGS.md). Consistent with c2: LLM inventories split too finely for BCubed.

claims.statement: Using the number of Wiktionary senses as k is systematically better than silhouette-chosen k (e.g. BERT-l-Wikt + 100 WikiBooks examples: 75.7 vs 74.5), and adding ~100-150 unlabeled corpus examples per lemma before clustering helps more than LLM-generated (45k+) or Wiktionary examples. Best test system (Wiktionary used three ways) 76.0 vs 1cpl 74.4.
claims.scope: Tables 4-6; dev numbers except Table 6; no significance tests for these.

our_assessment.why: Differences of 0.5-1.6 points on one dataset without significance tests; the direction (external k beats internal k; more unlabeled context helps) is what matters for arena-lsc: it motivates testing an LLM-supplied k on the XL-LEXEME tree (InventoryBreadth H3b) and augmenting each target's usages with unlabeled ones.

checked.result: 1cpl rows of Tables 3 and 6 reproduce (73.6/65.7/80.0/75.2 dev; 74.5 test vs 74.4); 1cpex 0.2-0.5 below print
1cpl / 1cpex per POS and split; decomposition: mono share 28.1% of dev instances, 1cpl on polysemous lemmas 63.4 dev / 65.2 test

relations.why: Both evaluate WSI with BCubed-family metrics; this one shows the trivial baseline's strength depends on the share of monosemous lemmas.

open_questions: Why is 1cpex 0.2-0.5 below the printed values (multiword lemmas? lexsn vs wnsn as gold key?)
Does an LLM-supplied k (number of induced senses) do for embedding clustering what Wiktionary's k does here? Tested in arena-lsc ticket 2026-11-06-InventoryBreadth H3.
